newsitem.title: USA: Talks break off between supermarket chains, union.
newsitem.headline: Talks break off between supermarket chains, union.

text.p: Talks broke off on Saturday between a negotiating committee for five supermarket chains in metropolitan New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania and a union representing 28,000 workers, hours before the current contract was due to expire.
A four-year contract between Shop-Rite, Pathmark, Grand Union, Foodtown and Edwards Super Food Stores and Local 1262, United Food and Commercial Workers Union was to expire at midnight EDT.

Union spokesman Frank Margiotta said, "We had come into negotiations this morning with the intent of staying right up to midnight." He said the interruption in talks was due to "impatience on the part of management."
He added that a strike such as occurred four years ago for 28 days was now more likely. Any strike could not occur for 10 days after the expiration of the contract.
Donald Vaillancourt, a Grand Union vice president, said negotiations were not hostile, and "We ended (the talks) today because we felt we had achieved all we were going to achieve."
"It's not management that goes on strike," Vaillancourt added.

He said the two sides had made some progress on the main issues and said the negotiations did not end on a hostile note. He said the main areas of contention were wages, pension funding and staffing flexibility on night and Sunday shifts.
Margiotta said wages and pension improvements were the two main areas of contention.

Both sides agreed that talks will resume on Monday but disagreed on the tone. Vaillancourt said there was a chance to resolve all remaining issues, but Margiotta said it was "the last realistic chance" to avoid starting the strike process with membership votes on Tuesday and on Wednesday.
"This break creates tension among the membership," he said.
